hero.lead: A nation of 68.7 million with farmland across half its land, whose Treasury plans €310 billion of medium and long-term debt in 2026, net of buybacks.

capital.heading: A Treasury the world lends to, and a living income for all.

register.name: Caisse des Dépôts sustainable bond, 2031
register.detail: Caisse des Dépôts · priced 21 April 2026 · due 25 February 2031 · 9 basis points above the OAT curve · order book €3.2bn from more than 83 investors
register.note: Its tenth ESG-labelled bond since 2017, under its Green, Social or Sustainable Financing Framework updated in July 2025
register.text: A five-year sustainable bond of the Caisse des Dépôts, the public financial institution, issued under its Green, Social or Sustainable Financing Framework. The current portfolio of eligible assets is 46% social housing, 34% green real estate and 12% renewable energy; the social housing serves the shelter standard.

register.name: Green OAT 3.80% 25 June 2037
register.detail: Agence France Trésor · syndicated 14 April 2026 · settlement 21 April 2026 · coupon 3.80% · yield 3.899% · demand above €113bn
register.note: A new green OAT with a shorter maturity than the existing nominal green OATs; green OATs outstanding stood at €105.7bn on 15 August 2026
register.text: A new green sovereign bond of €10 billion maturing on 25 June 2037, placed by syndication with total demand of more than €113 billion. Green OATs target State budget spending dedicated to mitigating climate change, adapting to its impacts, protecting biodiversity and preventing pollution.

register.name: State financing programme, 2026
register.detail: Agence France Trésor · indicative programme of 30 December 2025 · 71.2% complete at 31 July 2026, €220.8bn issued net of buybacks · index-linked bonds about 10%
register.note: Medium and long-term issues net of buybacks; €244.7bn issued gross and €23.8bn bought back at 31 July 2026
register.text: The Republic’s plan for medium and long-term borrowing in 2026: OATs and index-linked OATs of €310 billion net of buybacks, with bonds linked to French and European inflation about 10% of the total. At 31 July 2026 the Treasury had completed 71.2% of the programme, according to its monthly bulletin of August 2026.

register.name: Recovery and resilience plan
register.detail: European Commission · Recovery and Resilience Facility · grants €40.3bn, no loans · Council approval 13 July 2021 · updated 14 July 2023 with REPowerEU · fifth and final payment request of €6.1bn assessed positively 29 September 2026
register.note: All 176 milestones and targets fulfilled, as the Commission assessed; the final €6.1bn was reported paid on 30 October 2026
register.text: EU grants under NextGenerationEU for reforms and investments agreed with France, paid in instalments against milestones and targets; 49.5% of the plan supports climate objectives and 21.6% the digital transition. Its measures include the energy renovation of public and private buildings and investment in hospitals and health facilities, which serve the shelter, energy and health standards.

register.name: Bordeaux University Hospital modernisation, first phase
register.detail: European Investment Bank · loan signed at the end of 2025 · announced 8 July 2026 · first phase of a 2024–2029 programme · 18 projects of the property master plan
register.note: The first EIB loan to the hospital
register.text: An EIB loan to the Centre Hospitalier Universitaire de Bordeaux for the renovation, refurbishment and extension of its sites and for new buildings, with medical and non-medical equipment, IT and the energy efficiency of its buildings. It serves the health standard.

register.name: Intermediate rental housing, CDC Habitat, second tranche
register.detail: European Investment Bank · signed 30 June 2026 · announced 3 July 2026 · second tranche of a €500M envelope approved in 2025 · about 3,470 homes
register.note: A first tranche of €250M was paid out in 2025
register.text: EIB finance for the CDC Habitat group to build about 3,470 energy-efficient intermediate rental homes, let under income conditions, mainly in cities where rents are under strong pressure. They house middle-income households, young workers and essential workers, and serve the shelter standard.

register.name: Project 40, support for vulnerable youth and families (Apprentis d’Auteuil)
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · approved 19 June 2026 · borrower Fondation Apprentis d’Auteuil · redevelopment of its historic site in Paris
register.note: News reports that the loan was signed in October 2026 beside a €40M EIB loan, with an InvestEU guarantee
register.text: A CEB loan to the Fondation Apprentis d’Auteuil to increase the capacity, quality and sustainability of its social, educational and housing facilities for vulnerable children, teenagers and young adults. It serves the shelter and education standards.

register.name: Access to healthcare, social services and education (Crédit Coopératif)
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · approved June 2026 · one of fourteen loans totalling €1.2bn · news of 19 June 2026
register.note: Approved in the same round as the Apprentis d’Auteuil loan
register.text: A CEB loan to Crédit Coopératif that will improve access to affordable healthcare, social services, education and professional development. It serves the health, education and livelihood standards.

register.name: Specific housing and child protection (Caisse des Dépôts)
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · signed 11 March 2026 · borrower Caisse des Dépôts, for the Banque des Territoires · CEB support for its initiatives now €650M
register.note: Earlier CEB loans of 2016–2021 co-financed more than 15,000 places in care facilities
register.text: A CEB loan package to the Caisse des Dépôts to finance, through the Banque des Territoires, facilities for children in care and the building, renovation and adaptation of housing for people in severe hardship, women who are victims of violence, dependent elderly people, persons with disabilities, and students and young workers of limited means. It serves the shelter standard for those furthest from it.

register.name: In’li energy efficiency renovation programme
register.detail: European Investment Bank · project 20240449 · signed 17 December 2025 · total cost about €125M · about 25 residential buildings
register.note: About 2,700 affordable homes for middle-income households in the Île-de-France region
register.text: An EIB loan to In’li, an affordable housing provider in the Île-de-France region, for the energy renovation of about 25 residential buildings with some 2,700 homes for middle-income households, to lower their energy use and carbon emissions. It serves the shelter and energy standards.

register.name: Intermediate housing refinancing line (Banque des Territoires)
register.detail: European Investment Bank · signed 24 September 2025, at the HLM congress of the Union sociale pour l’habitat · fixed-rate loan in two tranches of €250M
register.note: Towards a national target of 75,000 intermediate rental homes to be built in 2024–2026
register.text: A new EIB loan refinancing line, distributed by the Banque des Territoires, for the building of intermediate rental homes for households that struggle to house themselves on the private market and are not eligible for social housing. It serves the shelter standard.

register.name: European Social Fund Plus, 2021–2027
register.detail: European Commission · Partnership Agreement with France adopted, 2 June 2022 · part of €18.4bn of cohesion policy funding for 2021–2027
register.note: Jobs, skills and training, and the fight against poverty and social exclusion, including food and material assistance
register.text: The European Social Fund Plus share of France’s €18.4 billion of cohesion policy funding for 2021–2027. It supports access to the job market, skills, training and career guidance, and the fight against poverty and social exclusion, with food and material assistance, including to children; it serves the livelihood standard, the one furthest from reach, and the food standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.
items.alt: Wheat and sunflower fields with hedgerows and a stone farmhouse at evening in the French countryside, France

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.
items.alt: An oak and beech forest in autumn light with a mossy floor and a quiet track, France

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 16.2% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.
items.alt: A tree-lined boulevard with café terraces and cream stone buildings in Paris in morning light, France

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.
items.alt: The wide Loire river at dawn with pale sandbanks and poplars along its banks, France

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.
items.alt: A hydroelectric dam and turquoise reservoir among Alpine peaks, with power lines in the valley below, France

items.name: Groupe Ares
items.text: A group of work-integration enterprises that has fought social and professional exclusion for more than 30 years, giving people in severe exclusion paid work with social and professional support; it supports more than 2,000 people each year, and 65% to 67% have left for a job or training in recent years.

items.name: Envie
items.text: A network of 53 enterprises and associations that collect, repair, refurbish and resell household appliances through work-integration jobs: 3,000 of its 3,780 employees are in work integration, for thirteen months on average, and its school trains them in logistics, repair and sales.

items.name: Phenix
items.text: A B Corp-certified company founded in 2014 whose digital tools keep unsold food and other goods from going to waste, connecting a network of 12,000 merchants and 1,500 partner associations; it reports saving more than 70 tonnes of products a day and 150 million meals since its creation.

items.name: Foncière d’Habitat et Humanisme
items.text: A solidarity property company of the Habitat et Humanisme movement, created in 1986 and approved as an ESUS social enterprise, that buys and renovates homes for people in difficulty, financed by solidarity investment from 11,246 shareholders; it let 6,235 homes at the end of 2025 and raised €21.8 million in 2025.

items.name: Siel Bleu
items.text: An association founded in Strasbourg in 1997 that brings adapted physical activity to older people, people with chronic illness or disabilities and people losing their autonomy, with nearly 115,000 participants each week at 10,000 places in France; the Banque des Territoires has invested €1 million in its associative bonds.

items.name: Simplon
items.text: An ESUS-approved training enterprise of the social and solidarity economy, at work since 2013, that makes digital skills and trades accessible to all, open notably to the long-term unemployed, older workers, refugees and people with disabilities; it has trained more than 40,000 people on 120 campuses in France and 24 countries, with 75.2% positive outcomes after training.
